items.title: Networking: wire ICE peer candidate exchange
items.detail: Milestone 4 ICE-candidate transport. Exchange the remote peer candidate set through a separately typed, signed, fresh presence/group payload with bounded counts, canonical address validation, credentials, generation, expiry, replacement, and teardown. Feed only the candidate/probe orchestrator. Never format an ICE candidate as the authority match-server route and never pass it directly to netStartClient. Close with focused validation plus ordinary peers across real NAT conditions.

items.title: Networking: publish STUN reflexive to peer
items.detail: Milestone 4 STUN candidate transport. Publish each peer own reflexive candidate as a separately typed, signed, fresh candidate record and consume the remote peer record only inside traversal. Distinguish local discovery, remote candidate, and elected authority match-server route at the type boundary. Reject stale, self, malformed, replayed, or identity-mismatched records and prove real-NAT behavior without a probe-to-netStartClient handoff.

items.title: Networking: UPnP map p2p probe ports
items.detail: Milestone 4 UPnP transport lifecycle. Discover, map, renew, replace, and unmap only the explicit sockets required by the candidate/traversal architecture, with bounded lease behavior and interface-change cleanup. Advertise results only as typed signed candidates. The elected authority separately publishes its validated ENet match-server route after listen startup; UPnP discovery or probe success can never synthesize that route.

items.title: Networking: replace kbps placeholder measurement
items.detail:
Passive prior/current-session upload measurement is now production-connected. The client samples cumulative real ENet sent bytes over completed two-second windows, requires 4096 bytes, persists the best fresh lower bound for 30 days, and signs it in presence v4. Remote reports expire after 90 seconds. Group authority uses highest fresh kbps, match initiator on exact/no-data ties, then smallest public handle; TURN consumes the same fresh reports and removes stale/dropped/failed candidates.

Verification: isolated client/updater/tests compile PASS; [t-networking-004] 37 assertions/5 cases; full pd-tests 56,664/1,036; ordinary two-process results-20260812T151813Z.json PASS 23/23 with host/client real-match measurements 64/32 kbps persisted in each isolated pd.ini and clean exits.

Boundary: this item closes the measurement placeholder and its signed election/relay input. Automatic live listen-host migration and the broader P2P-to-ENet endpoint handoff remain T-NETWORKING-008/T-NETWORKING-006.

items.title: Networking: add TURN public relay fallback
items.detail: Milestone 4 relay fallback. Define a configurable authenticated public TURN service, credential rotation, capacity and abuse limits, typed signed relay candidates, expiry, health, teardown, and user-visible failure. A relay descriptor remains candidate/orchestration data, not a match-server route. Complete only when ordinary peers can reach the elected server-authoritative listen match through the relay path with protocol, identity, catalog, and rollback validation intact.

items.title: Networking: unify legacy hole-punch with tier machine
items.detail: Milestone 4 traversal consolidation after candidate semantics are correct. Retire overlapping legacy hole-punch ownership and leave one bounded candidate/probe orchestrator with explicit attempt, timeout, cancellation, replacement, and teardown states. Preserve D-003 as a separate authority route plane: exactly one authority starts its listen host and publishes the typed signed server route; non-authorities perform one idempotent join. Candidate, probe, and relay outputs cannot call netStartClient directly.

items.title: Decide whether Queue Match state is host-local or network-synchronized
items.detail: Queue Match is an additive playlist feature, not part of D-004 base-game plus Theater scope. Defer the host-local versus synchronized queue decision until after 1.0. T-INPUT-002 remains the implementation placeholder; no release milestone depends on either item.

options.label: Host-local queue (no net message)
options.tradeoff: Queue Match is a host-convenience feature; the host cycles settings as matches end and clients simply load whatever the next match is. Simplest to ship, no protocol change, fits the P3-deferred scope. The queued-count badge is host-screen-only; joined clients cannot see how many matches are queued or what is coming. No SVC_QUEUE_STATE, no protocol bump, no resync-path changes.

options.label: Networked queue (SVC_QUEUE_STATE + protocol bump)
options.tradeoff: Every player sees the queued count and upcoming settings, which suits organized/tournament play and matches the 'badge displays queued count' intent for all participants. Adds a new SVC_QUEUE_STATE message, a NET_PROTOCOL_VER increment (must update g_TestExpectedNetProtocolVer in tests/test_versions.cpp in the same change per the silent-bump guard), queue state in the resync path, and a larger test surface.

options.tradeoff: Keep JSON plus INI, but add candidate preparation, a journal or equivalent crash recovery, complete rollback, and coherent copy/delete. Smaller schema migration, permanent cross-file lifecycle complexity.
